\title{A One-Scale Positive-Kernel $K+R$ Basin Criterion}
\author{}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We derive an exact composition law for a comparison-controlled reference
channel and a state-weighted residual channel.  Combining the local-cylinder
comparison with Gaussian concentration yields a nonempty numerical budget
inside the sharp nonlinear radius.  The remaining task is to realize the two
subkernels for the complete nonlinear $SU(2)$ conditional measure.
\end{abstract}

\section{Composition theorem}
Let $K_0,K,R$ be positive bad subkernels on a retained-state space, and let
$V>0$.

\begin{theorem}
If
\[
 K\le e^\ell K_0,
 \qquad K_0V\le kV,
 \qquad RV\le rV,
\]
then
\[
 (K+R)V\le (e^\ell k+r)V.
\]
In particular, the Stage 19 connected-cluster theorem applies whenever
\[
 e^\ell k+r<e^{-\alpha}\Delta^{-2}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Positivity permits the three inequalities to be applied without cancellation:
$KV\le e^\ell K_0V\le e^\ell kV$, and addition gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\section{Feasible local radius}
Let $\delta(r)$ be the Stage 21 local Gaussian union upper bound and let
$\ell(r)$ be the Stage 23 comparison loss per extension.  We select $r$ so
that
\[
 e^{\ell(r)}\delta(r)=\frac{q_{\rm target}}2,
 \qquad q_{\rm target}=0.002430277501841998.
\]
Monotonicity on the certified interval and bisection give
\[
 r_*=0.00614955590043087.
\]
This is only $53.69\%$ of the sharp nonlinear maximum
$0.011453785959974176$.

\section{Frontier}
The budget polytope is nonempty.  This is stronger than merely observing
overlap of local radii: it allocates explicit room to both reference and
charged residual channels.  However, the complete nonlinear conditional
measure has not yet been decomposed into physical $K$ and $R$ satisfying the
hypotheses.  The residual weighted partition numerator is the next estimate.
